note: Issue 388, patrons.md section 7. He introduces himself once, on arrival. The cooldown is longer than any run so that a man cannot introduce himself twice, and the condition is asked of the SENDER rather than of the colony - every other patron in the post is a different man with a different arrival, and a condition reading any arrival would have all of them introducing themselves on the month the third one came. Urgency in the middle: it is the first thing he ever sends and it asks for nothing, so it should not shoulder a demand off the desk.

Issue 388, patrons.md sections 4 and 10: every patron has this letter. Any patron may send it, at any regard - the gate it always had, since the offer model it once asked (PatronOffer, retired by #439) made a bare request unconditional. Cooldown 14, as the duke's is: a man who asked twice a year would be a tax rather than a character. Urgency below a duke's 0.7, because a patron is asking a favour and a duke is describing a difficulty he has.

Issue 388, patrons.md section 8. Fires once, the month he gives notice, and the cooldown is longer than any run because a man gives notice once. High urgency: it is the month a closing window opens and the PC cannot act on a deadline he was not told about. patron_leaving had been emitted since #283 and read by nothing.

Issue 396, policy.md section 8. A patron whose specialty is resources or livestock offers to turn his Barony's market toward the colony for that kind: the Crown's price for it rises while the policy stands. Not while he already carries one. Cooldown 24: a second offer inside two years would be a standing discount rather than a favour.

Issue 395, patrons.md section 5. A patron whose specialty is the rivals offers to trouble the duke nearest to war who can still be troubled. Cooldown 12: the trouble lasts a year, and a man who offered it again while it ran would be offering nothing.

Issue 440, patrons.md section 4, policy.md section 4. The Steward's renegotiation, from a patron: a policy of his that the PC is not paying for has run past his patience, and he names the month he lets it go. Urgency and cooldown as the Steward's, because it is the same warning and the ending it warns of is sooner than most.

Issue 441, patrons.md section 4. Every patron asks for his need, a resource or livestock kind that is never his specialty's. Not while anything the PC promised him is still outstanding: a man waiting on a ship does not write for another. Cooldown 12: a year's shipment is a year's favour, and asked for more often it would be a levy. Urgency just under his gold letter's, because a need met through two letters is the slower favour.
